description:
About us: We are a duo passionate about technology and science, focused on creating practical, high-impact solutions for education.

The Project (Artemis Outpost 2026): We are participating in the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge with an educational simulator (Hardcore Tycoon). We use real NASA mission data (like the LRO) to teach thermodynamics, physics, and engineering in an immersive and interactive way for students and schools.
summary:
The Simulator Outpost Lunar (Artemis Outpost 2026) is an interactive web-based educational simulator focused on STEM education, developed using modern technologies such as HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and Three.js. The project recreates the strategic management of a permanent lunar base at Shackleton Crater (Lunar South Pole), integrating data and scientific guidelines from NASA missions and APIs, such as topographic mapping from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), metabolic parameters from the Human Research Program (HRP), and space weather monitoring from DONKI.
The simulator addresses the challenge of engaging students in aerospace engineering by combining the rigorous management of vital resources (energy, oxygen, water, and regolith), 3D pressurized module construction, and dynamic operational minigames challenged by real space events, such as solar storms and meteor showers.
Its importance lies in democratizing access to advanced aerospace concepts through a playful, immersive, and high-fidelity technical experience, strengthening critical thinking and preparing young talents for the challenges of sustainable space exploration.
details:
The Simulator Outpost Lunar (Artemis Outpost 2026) is an interactive web-based educational simulator designed for STEM learning in a tycoon format, placing the user in command of the first permanent lunar base at Shackleton Crater located at the Lunar South Pole. Operating in strategic turns, commanders must manage vital resources including energy, oxygen, water, and regolith, construct 3D pressurized modules, advance through a technology tree, and overcome random space events such as solar storms and meteorite impacts via surface operational minigames.

This project facilitates the learning of advanced aerospace engineering, science, and sustainability concepts in an engaging and interactive way while stimulating critical thinking, risk management, and problem-solving under strict resource constraints, offering high accessibility by running directly in modern web browsers without heavy installations. Its intended impact is to inspire the next generation of students and young talent to pursue careers in STEM fields and space exploration by translating complex space agency data into interactive and understandable experiences for young audiences.

The project is built using HTML5, JavaScript, and CSS3, styled with Tailwind CSS for a modern and responsive interface inspired by NASA control panels, and powered by the Three.js r128 engine for real-time rendering of the interactive Moon model, topographic textures, and base structures or vehicles, utilizing official data and guidelines from NASA missions and APIs including LRO for topography, HRP for life support, and DONKI for space weather monitoring.

The creative aspect of the project lies in the fusion of an interactive 3D orbital Moon viewer with an educational tycoon simulation, allowing users to observe the direct impact of engineering choices such as hydroponic greenhouses and nuclear reactors on a rotating celestial body, complemented by customizable avatars and an immersive Web Audio API soundscape. Key considerations during development included ensuring scientific rigor so that metabolic rates, lunar South Pole challenges, and space phenomena accurately reflect real NASA data, maintaining usability and accessibility through a scroll-free single-screen layout to prevent visual clipping alongside automatic tactical alerts and an integrated visual tutorial, and carefully balancing turn-based difficulties and strict inventory validations to create a rewarding and glitch-free experience.
